verification.notes: Fallback is position-complete: the inserted mutual 12-month-fee cap plus the added gross negligence / wilful misconduct exclusions combine with the retained Sections 13 and 14 carve-out to cover all six fallback elements. Preferred is not reached: no USD 1,000,000 alternative limb, no data protection/security carve-out, no fraud carve-out, no express carve-out for infringement of the other party's IP, and no statement that Customer's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. Placement is sound — the cap is added inside Section 15 so the pre-existing sentence "The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14" governs the new cap; no dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence results. Minimality holds: two sentences added, nothing deleted or paraphrased, no survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories or procedural boilerplate; the second sentence reuses the existing carve-out formula rather than duplicating it. Intent preserved: the mutual consequential-damages exclusion, the direct-damages exclusive-remedy sentence and the risk-allocation recital survive unchanged, and the fee basis tracks the existing Fee Schedule. Actionable note (rationale only, not a fallback defect): the unqualified mutual cap on "total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement" could be read to cap Customer's own obligation to pay fees; if raising to preferred, add "Customer's obligation to pay fees is not subject to this cap" together with the USD 1,000,000 floor and the data protection/security, fraud and other-party-IP carve-outs.

That fails the fallback (mutual successor assignment on written notice; other assignments subject to consent not unreasonably withheld) and, as to Section 3(c), approaches walk-away territory (blanket prohibition on Customer assignment with no M&A carve-out). verification.notes: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: mutual successor assignment on written notice, all other assignments subject to consent not unreasonably withheld. Preferred level is not reached: no affiliate carve-out for Customer, the successor right is mutual (so Vendor can assign without Customer consent), and there is no bar on assignment to a Customer competitor. If the preferred position is pursued, add (i) "Sparkling may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets", (ii) restrict the consent-free successor right to Sparkling only, and (iii) add "and in no event to a competitor of Sparkling". The deletion of "assign this Agreement or" from Section 3(c) is necessary, not cosmetic: retained, that covenant would flatly contradict the new mutual successor right and reinstate a blanket prohibition on Customer assignment. The remainder of 3(c) (transfer, lease, export, sublicence of the Work) is preserved intact and reads grammatically within the covenant list. No dangling cross-references or undefined terms result; the change-of-control analysis is unaffected because the Agreement contains no such trigger. Minor drafting note only (not a level failure): the rewrite of 20(d) drops the original words "or any rights and obligations under this Agreement". "Any other assignment" should be read to capture partial transfers, but if the counterparty may argue otherwise, restore breadth with "any other assignment or transfer of rights or obligations requires the written consent of the other party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld."

verification.notes: All ten preferred elements are met in operative language by the single inserted paragraph: defend/indemnify/hold harmless for Customer and affiliates, the four trigger limbs (IP allegation, breach of law, Vendor-caused unauthorised access/disclosure, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), the notice/control/cooperation procedure, and an express cap on any Customer-side indemnity. The preferred level is therefore position-complete and the finding is correctly classified as a deviation targeting the preferred position. The fallback level is not complete (no refund backstop where procure/modify/replace fail; no 3x super-cap), but that is immaterial because only one level need be met — and the drafter's choice not to import the super-cap is sound, since Section 15 already disapplies the liability limitation to Section 13, leaving the indemnity uncapped in Customer's favour. Minimality holds: nothing existing is deleted or paraphrased, the favourable retained (a)-(c) remedies and the uncapped Section 15 carve-out survive, and the insertion adds no survival tail, expense allocation, extra damages categories or procedures beyond the notice/control/cooperation mechanic the checklist requires. Reuse of the defined term "Losses" avoids introducing a new damages basis, and referencing "Sparkling's data or Confidential Information" is justified because the agreement defines no "Customer Data" term. Intent is preserved: no dangling cross-reference or undefined term is created (Work, Maintenance Services, Losses and Confidential Information are existing contract terms), the ten-day notice condition on the original warranty-breach indemnity is untouched and operates alongside the new procedure, and the Section 15 exclusive-remedy/consequential-damages allocation is unchanged. Drafting note for the drafter (not a defect at the targeted level): the new paragraph's unqualified "Sparkling shall notify Garman of any such claim" sits next to the retained ten-calendar-day notice condition; if Vendor argues the ten-day condition applies to the new limbs, consider an express "promptly (and the ten-day condition above shall not apply to this paragraph)" clarifier in negotiation.

verification.notes: The finding is correctly classified as missing: existing Sections 17(b), 17(c), 16 and 18 only require Sparkling to return Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes, and impose no exit assistance or data-return duty on Garman. All six preferred elements are carried by the single inserted Section 17(d); no element is left to the margin comment or to an undefined trigger. Minimality holds: the redline is one concise inserted paragraph in the termination section, with no deletion or paraphrase of retained language (17(b), the default/perpetual-licence sentence and the survival provision are untouched) and no extras such as survival tails, at-own-expense wording or added remedies. verification.notes: Fallback checklist is complete: the retained one-year Software-to-Specifications warranty covers the ≥90-day software element, and the two inserted sentences supply the 30-day services warranty and the repair/replacement/refund remedy that the Agreement previously lacked (Section 10(c) repair was a maintenance obligation, not a warranty remedy). Preferred level is not reached: the services warranty is 30 days rather than 90, and there is no compliance-with-applicable-laws warranty and no no-malicious-code warranty. To move to preferred the drafter would need to change "thirty (30) calendar days" to "ninety (90) days" and add express law-compliance and malicious-code warranties. Minimality holds: two inserted sentences tracking the playbook model language, no deletions, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural extras, and the favourable existing one-year (and continuing) Software warranty and the Section 10(c) no-charge repair obligation are left intact. The "professional and workmanlike" standard in the services sentence is the necessary substantive content of a services warranty, not an extra. Intent is preserved: no defined term, cross-reference or commercial mechanic is disturbed; the fee-charging carve-out in Section 10(c) and the Fee Schedule reference survive unchanged. One drafting caution (not a failure): Section 12 covers "the acceptance period", and the retained acceptance/rejection remedy in Sections 7–8 is stated to be "in lieu of any other remedy", so consider opening the inserted remedy sentence with "Except as provided in Sections 7 and 8," to avoid any argument of overlap during acceptance. Note that the remedy election sits "at Garman's option", which matches the playbook model language but is the vendor-favourable variant; it does not defeat the remedy elements.

verification.notes: The rule is correctly classified as missing: the rendered operative language shows no pre-existing insurance covenant in the General Matters provisions, and the vendor installs Software and converts data at Authorized Locations, so the absence is walk-away territory. Fallback level is complete: both atomic elements (E&O not less than USD 1,000,000; cyber and privacy not less than USD 2,000,000) appear as an unconditional Vendor covenant in operative text, not merely promised in the margin comment. Preferred level is not complete — CGL per-occurrence and aggregate limits, E&O at USD 2,000,000, cyber at USD 5,000,000, workers' compensation and certificates on request are all absent. To reach preferred, the drafter would need to add CGL USD 1,000,000 per occurrence / USD 2,000,000 aggregate, raise E&O to USD 2,000,000, raise cyber to USD 5,000,000, add statutory workers' compensation, and add a certificates-on-request sentence. Minimality holds: the insertion is a single sentence limited to the two selected fallback elements. It correctly omits model-language extras that the fallback checklist does not require — 'at its own expense', the term-plus-one-year survival tail, CGL, and the certificate mechanic — each of which would have been a non-minimal addition. No existing wording (including the assignment and headings provisions) was deleted or paraphrased. Intent is preserved: the new covenant is a standalone obligation that creates no undefined terms, no dangling cross-references, and no contradiction with retained assignment, installation, or interpretation language; unrelated allocation, timing and commercial mechanics survive intact.
